- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to over-forecast, especially in early/medium horizon; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% if sentiment >0.75.
- If sentiment drops to 0.00 or near 0.00, model often under-responds; increase forecast by 10–20% for early horizon if sentiment <0.33.
- Overshoots after spikes (e.g., 30d forecast >10.0) are common when sentiment was high; cap forecast at 2x prior 18d average if sentiment >0.75.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast >1.5x prior 18d mean, reduce by 20–40% if sentiment <0.50.
- Horizon-specific: 30d forecasts are prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment drops sharply, adjust 30d forecast downward by 10–30% within 3–5 days of sentiment change.
- Avoid forecasting spikes >2.5x prior 18d max unless sentiment >0.80; otherwise, apply smoothing filter to prevent runaway growth.
